title: The Listening Hymn
premise: Ivo Kavanagh, a hospice nurse who has spent his career dismissing the strange habit of the dying to count backwards, returns to his hometown of Hollowmere when the town's last founding resident, Edith Marlowe, signs herself into hospice care. Waiting on her porch is Wren, the imaginary friend Ivo abandoned at age nine — unchanged, patient, and no longer imaginary. Wren reveals that Hollowmere's founders bound something beneath the town with a ritual called the Listening Hymn, renewed each generation by a signer's death, and that Ivo, as the heir of the family that broke the chain in 1974, must finish what they started before Edith signs the final papers and releases it. Torn between loyalty to the dying woman who raised him and the truth of what his grandfather did, Ivo completes the hymn at terrible cost: he takes Wren's place as the listener, becoming the town's new guardian — present, faithful, and no longer entirely human.
about_author: Isandro Ravensworth is the pen name of a former palliative care chaplain who spent eleven years sitting with the dying and swears half of them were counting down to something. The Listening Hymn is their third novel, written in a house at the edge of a town that does not appear on all maps.

chapters.title: The Counting Ward
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At St. Brigid's hospice, Ivo charts his patients' eerie habit of counting backwards from numbers only they know. When Mr. Aldous reaches zero and dies mid-syllable, Ivo documents it as terminal lucidity. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking at the edges; the reader sees what Ivo refuses to.

chapters.title: Papers from Hollowmere
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A lawyer arrives with documents: Edith Marlowe, the woman who fostered Ivo after his parents' deaths, has requested him personally for her final weeks. Attached is an old photograph of the Hollowmere founders, one face scratched out. Beat: dread disguised as obligation; Ivo accepts because refusing feels like betrayal.

chapters.title: The Porch
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Ivo arrives in Hollowmere after nineteen years. On Edith's porch sits Wren — his childhood imaginary friend, feathered and wrong-jointed, exactly as left behind. Wren says only, 'You're late.' Beat: vertigo; the rational scaffolding of Ivo's life begins to groan.

chapters.title: Edith's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Edith is sharp, dying, and counting backwards from 400. She warns Ivo never to answer Wren aloud and never to read the founders' ledger in the cellar. That night Ivo hears the whole town humming one note. Beat: love entangled with secrecy; Edith knows more than she'll say.

chapters.title: What Wren Was For
chapters.summary: POV Ivo, interwoven with childhood memory. Flashbacks reveal nine-year-old Ivo inventing Wren the week his grandfather drowned — or didn't. Wren explains he was never invented; he was assigned, a listener sent to watch the Kavanagh line. Beat: grief reframed; the imaginary friend was a warden.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Cellar
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Disobeying Edith, Ivo finds the founders' ledger: seven names, seven signatures renewed by death, and his grandfather's line torn out mid-word. Beneath the house, something answers when he reads aloud. Beat: curiosity punished; the inheritance is a debt.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Sings
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The town gathers for Sunday service where the congregation sings the Listening Hymn without knowing why. Pastor Grell's sermon slips into the backwards count. Ivo realizes every resident is an unwitting chorus holding the thing below. Beat: communal complicity; horror wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Sixth Signer
chapters.summary: POV Edith. In her voice, we learn 1974: six founders signed, the seventh — Ivo's grandfather — refused, and the ritual has been fraying for fifty years. Edith has kept the town alive by dying slowly enough to hold the papers unsigned. Beat: sacrifice revealed; her stubbornness was armor.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Wren offers a deal: finish the hymn, sign nothing, and Wren will take the burden himself as he was originally meant to. But Wren's terms require Ivo to let Edith die unconfessed. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy; loyalty and truth pull apart.

chapters.title: Aldous Reaches Zero
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Back at the hospice wing, another patient counts to zero days early and the lights fail across Hollowmere. In the dark, Ivo sees the shape beneath the town through the floorboards — vast, listening back. Beat: first direct contact; denial becomes impossible.

chapters.title: The Scratched Face
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Researching the founders' photograph, Ivo identifies the scratched-out face: not his grandfather, but Edith's twin sister, Lark, erased from every record. Edith catches him and finally begins, haltingly, to tell the truth. Beat: the past exhumes itself; trust rebuilt on broken ground.

chapters.title: Lark's Verse
chapters.summary: POV Edith. Edith recounts how Lark wrote the hymn's missing final verse — the verse that doesn't bind the thing but frees it — and was made the eighth founder, the one who listens forever. Wren was Lark's gift to whoever came next. Beat: revelation; the monster may be a prisoner.

chapters.title: Grell's Congregation
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Pastor Grell, learning Ivo has the ledger, turns the town against him — a midnight congregation at his door, singing the hymn off-key, deliberately wrong, to hasten the release. Beat: justice outside the law; the mob believes it is protecting itself.

chapters.title: The Papers Unsigned
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Edith weakens fast; the lawyer presses her to sign the estate papers, which Ivo now understands are also the seventh signature. He forges a delay, betraying the lawyer's trust and risking Edith's anger. Beat: loyalty vs. truth sharpened into a single pen stroke.

chapters.title: Down Where It Listens
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Guided by Wren, Ivo descends through the cellar into the founders' sealed chamber and meets what Lark bound: not a devil, but the town's accumulated dead, still waiting for a verse of release. Beat: awe and pity; the horror grieves.

chapters.title: Edith Signs
chapters.summary: POV Edith. Too proud to be spared, Edith signs the papers while Ivo sleeps, choosing the town's old bargain over truth. The hum beneath Hollowmere rises to a chord. Beat: betrayal by love; the kindest person does the cruelest thing.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. With hours left, Ivo reconstructs Lark's final verse from the ledger, the hymn, and Wren's memory. Grell's congregation seals the church; Wren holds the door with his body, coming apart feather by feather. Beat: desperate assembly; everything Ivo disbelieved is now his only instrument.

chapters.title: The Listening Hymn
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In the chamber, Ivo sings the completed hymn as the dead rise around him and Edith's count reaches zero above. The binding breaks — but a listener must remain. Wren steps forward to take the place, as promised. Beat: climax; courage as song rather than violence.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Edith dies at zero, at peace, whispering Lark's name. The release takes the dead gently — except Wren, whose bargain fails because a volunteer cannot substitute for an heir. The listening turns toward Ivo. Beat: cost made real; mercy has fine print.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Ivo chooses to stay — not as a prisoner but as a keeper, singing the freed dead onward instead of binding them. Wren, released at last, dissolves into feathers and morning light. Beat: transfiguration; inheritance accepted on Ivo's own terms.

chapters.title: Morning Over Hollowmere
chapters.summary: POV Mara, a young hospice nurse newly arrived. Hollowmere is quiet, the hymn unsung, the town oddly light. On the porch of the Marlowe house she meets a kind caretaker named Kavanagh who asks her to listen carefully to the dying. Beat: bittersweet resolution; the cycle continues, changed.

chapters.title: Coda: Still Counting
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Weeks later, Mara's patients begin counting backwards, and she writes to no one about the man who told her every number ends somewhere worth arriving. In the last line, Ivo — listening always — finally stops counting himself. Beat: quiet closure; belief chosen freely at last.
